subject: Urgent: model variant rollout causing p95/p99 spikes for Oraclum
messages:
From: Lucia Gomez <lucia@oraclum.ai>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: ops@oraclum.ai
Date: 2028-05-30T01:48:00Z
Subject: Sudden latency spike after variant B rollout

Hi Ava / Hannah,

We pushed your recommended model variant B to 10% traffic at ~2028-05-30T01:15Z and immediately started seeing p95/p99 jumps across our production workload. P95 went from ~180ms to ~720ms, p99 to >2s, and we observed several 503s during the spike. Throughput dropped by ~25% during the window.

This is impacting our customer QA and some end-users are timing out. We rolled the split back to 0% on our side to mitigate but wanted to escalate — can you please advise next steps and whether you can roll back on your side? We attached our aggregated latency CSV and traces.

Thanks,
Lucia
Director of ML Ops, Oraclum

Attachments: oraclum_tail_latencies_20280530.csv, svc-traces-oraclum-20280530.zip
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Lucia Gomez <lucia@oraclum.ai>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-30T01:56:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike after variant B rollout

Hi Lucia — thank you for the flag and the traces, very helpful. Sorry for the disruption.

We're pulling SRE and product into the thread to triage. Initial asks: can you confirm whether the affected requests are mostly long-context chat sessions or short completion calls? Also, did you see any change in the request size distribution or concurrency from your side?

Dylan/Rishi — assigning for immediate investigation. Priority: determine whether this is a model execution performance regression, kernel fallback on some hardware paths, or something in the routing/serving layer. If it's service-side, we'll coordinate a rollback of variant B for Oraclum immediately.

I'll keep Lucia updated with our findings and timeline.

— Ava
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-30T02:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike after variant B rollout — initial SRE triage

Quick update from SRE triage: we correlated Oraclum's p95/p99 increase with a rollout event at 2028-05-30T01:14:47Z when variant B (v2-quant-fp16) started receiving 10% of traffic. Observations:

- Spike pattern: tail-heavy latency on tensors > 1k tokens and on requests hitting sequence length > 512.
- Error modes: transient 503 and occasional OOM-recovery retries on machines in the east-us-2 pool (A100s + mixed driver 535.x).
- Kernel behavior: there are repeated kernel fallback logs for the quantized execution path — seems like the optimized path is failing and hitting a slower emulated kernel for some ops.
- Resource signals: memory pressure and increased GPU memcpy stalls on a subset (~12%) of hosts serving variant B.

We pulled one affected host and attached core traces (svc-traces...). Early hypothesis: the variant's quantization profile triggers a less-common kernel path on drivers we haven't exercised recently; that path falls back to slow code causing tail latency and occasional OOM-triggered retries.

Immediate remediation options:
- Full rollback of variant B for Oraclum (fast, low risk).
- Reduce variant B traffic to 0% from the control plane and deploy a hotfix that forces an alternative kernel selection or revert quantization changes.

I'm standing by to execute whichever path product/exec prefers.

— Dylan
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, ava_chen@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-30T03:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike — recommended action

Thanks Dylan — based on the SRE notes, recommend immediate rollback of variant B for Oraclum from the control plane and open a hotfix branch to revert the aggressive quantization flags. The rollback should be scoped to the Oraclum routing rule only (do not affect global deploys). Steps:

1) Ava/Marissa: request rollback of variant B for Oraclum in the next 5 minutes and confirm traffic is back to baseline.
2) Dylan: capture full kernel logs and relay to model infra team; mark affected host IDs for a targeted kernel/driver repro.
3) Hannah/Marissa: coordinate post-rollback customer comms and offer a small credits package if needed.
4) Jonas: please prepare exec summary for leadership; I will drive the hotfix PR.

I'll stand up a quick A/B repro internally and share findings.

— Rishi
Product Manager, Model Serving
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: Lucia Gomez <lucia@oraclum.ai>
Date: 2028-05-30T03:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike after variant B rollout — rollback started

Performed rollback of variant B for Oraclum at 2028-05-30T03:09:27Z (control plane). Traffic is now routed to the previous stable variant. Monitoring dashboards show p95 returning toward baseline within one minute; p99 coming down but still noisy as existing in-flight requests drain.

Lucia — can you confirm whether you're observing improvements on your side? We will keep the variant disabled for Oraclum until root cause is fully identified.

Attachment: rollback-confirmation.txt (control-plane event id: evt-ORC-20280530-321)

— Ava
From: Lucia Gomez <lucia@oraclum.ai>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-30T03:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike after variant B rollout — rollback started

Confirming — latencies are trending back to expected ranges. P95 is ~200ms now; p99 ~420ms and still improving. Thank you for the quick response and rollback. We'll hold our side of the split disabled as well until we get a postmortem.

Appreciate the rapid handling.

— Lucia
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, ava_chen@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-30T06:12:00Z
Subject: Exec brief: Oraclum outage window and next steps

TL;DR: Variant B (v2-quant-fp16) triggered a tail-latency regression for Oraclum when routed on a subset of east-us-2 hosts. Customer-facing impact lasted ~15–20 minutes; rollback completed and metrics stabilized. Next steps and asks below.

Impact summary:
- Customer: Oraclum (DL-8721) — production p95/p99 elevated; throughput down ~25% during the window.
- Duration: ~01:14:47Z–03:09:27Z (init spike to rollback completion).
- Root cause hypothesis: quantization + driver/kernel fallback path on certain GPU host configurations.

Immediate asks (Owners):
- Rishi: lead hotfix branch to revert quant flags + regression test across driver matrix (due EOD).
- Dylan: collect repro hosts, attach kernel traces, and own the incident ticket (INF-4892).
- Marissa/Hannah: finalize customer comms + propose a one-time credit (sales + CS).
- Ava: update runbook to include a traffic-split kill-switch for variant-level rollouts.

We should also add a pre-rollout synthetic perf check against the full driver matrix for any quantized variants. Please treat this as high priority; I'll follow up with leadership once we have the postmortem and remediation plan.

— Jonas
VP, Product Operations
